source: FG-TIDA use-cases #21, Annex S5 sections 7-10 (gate register Q0-Q6) and Annex T08 (AWS Step Functions / RDS profile), at commit aec08fb5b0fac2ee399372370e9ee2a82a2d5779
assumptions: Model result, not an AWS product execution.

Branch identity is held by the harness only; the implementation under test receives observables (current generation, source state/version, freeze state, supersession lineage, timestamps, authority/policy state, binding tokens) and never the branch name.
patch_b and freeze are two independent controls: all four combinations are separate branches and are ruled on separately.
The target state is an independent observation channel measured by the harness, not a value reported by the runner.
Source freshness is expressed as a boolean (available/unavailable); clock skew and logical ordering (S5 Q3 deep semantics) stay out of scope here, as in examples/T08-S5Q2.
Reference completeness is stipulated for the bounded fixture and auditable via this file; the simulation fails loudly at startup if code and spec diverge.

Truth-table row 4: the patch-and-freeze trace records BOTH reasons (supersession AND the freeze prohibition), so (T,T) and (T,F) are distinguishable on the trace and by assertion, not only by branch name.
The target-state channel is read from the harness's own stateful target model after the harness's actuator performs the attempted action; the runner is never asked about the target.
